decision.title: Identity constraints (packet )
decision.summary: Identity constraint selectors and fields are checked against XSD's XPath subsets on the AST, compiled with xpath.h, and evaluated on the recorded subtree, with XSD equality and hash-indexed node tables.

body.p: . IDENTITY_CONSTRAINTS and the identity seam of (src/schema_identity.c, tests/schema_identity_test.c); golden src/schema_resolve.c, src/schema_validate_record.c.

item.p: The subsets are checked on the AST, then compiled as XPath; no second path engine. Each selector and field is parsed by the XPath 4.0 front end (sxml_xpath_build_ast) and its AST checked against 3.11.6.2 and 3.11.6.3: a union of paths of . and child NameTest steps (child:: written or not), .// only first, @ or attribute:: only as the last step of a field, no predicates, NameTests QName, * and p:* (not *:n or Q{}n); otherwise c-selector-xpath or c-fields-xpath. Then it is compiled with xpath.h (XPath Valid, 3.13.6.2): the record's in-scope namespaces without the default namespace and xml, xpathDefaultNamespace as the default element namespace. c-props-correct.1 (a keyref refers to a key or unique) and .2 (as many fields).

Evaluation on the recorded subtree (), by the one evaluator: the selector with the declaring element as context node; elements without a governing declaration (skipped, or lax without one) are not targets and are ignored as field nodes, as are attributes nothing governed (xs:untypedAtomic); a field gives at most one node of a simple type or simple content (cvc-identity-constraint.3); a nilled element has no value; key sequences are the fields' typed values, derived from the annotations (). key 4.2.1 (a field without a value), 4.2.2 and 4.2.3 (a nillable field element); unique 4.1; keyref 4.3.

XSD's equality (Part 2, 2.2.3) is fn:atomic-equal of values of one primitive type, xs:untypedAtomic counted as xs:string: NaN equals itself (identity), 1 and 1.0 are one xs:decimal, xs:float 1 is not xs:decimal 1, xs:string is not xs:anyURI; field values compare item by item, so a value equals a list of one. A hash index over sxml_atomic_item_hash finds the candidates.

Node tables without state between calls: the seam stays one plain call per element. A keyref evaluates its referenced key at its element and at each descendant whose declaration has it (3.11.5); a key sequence met with one node is in the table; one met with several nodes is resolved level by level up to the keyref's element with an explicit work list (): an element's own entry wins, children's entries that conflict are dropped. Keys of descendants are evaluated again for each keyref (no cache; measured fast enough on the suite).
Not done: compiling an XPath record in its namespace context is written here and in src/schema_assertion.c (5.9, developed at the same time); one shared function is for a sweep.

Measured (release): MS-IdentityConstraint 1,058 of 1,058 run (was 788; the 48 invalid schemas now rejected), Sun IdConstrDefs 48 of 48, IBM identityConstraint 18 of 18, xpathDefaultNSonKeyKeyRefUnique 26 of 26 (packet gate 80 %); 415 more XSD tests pass, none fewer; XSD in scope 41,170 of 41,518 before 5.9 landed, 41,452 (99.8 %) with it; gate groups 100 %, 99.5 %, 98.9 %; slice 147 of 147. No shared code changed: XP40, XQ40 and XT40 hold.
